concepts.title: Indexing Characters in a String
concepts.definition: Square-bracket indexing reaches any single character of a string: positions count from 0 on the left up to length minus 1, and negative positions count backwards from -1 on the right down to minus the length; an out-of-range position raises IndexError.
concepts.key_idea: The mirror rule is simple: position i from the left equals position i minus size from the right.

solution_steps.explain: Backward counting starts at minus the size.

concepts.title: Slice Length Arithmetic
concepts.definition: The slice str1[n:m] copies characters from position n up to but excluding m, so the copy always holds m minus n characters; a third value k keeps only every k-th one, and the kept count rounds the span up over k.
concepts.key_idea: A first index larger than the second yields an empty string, and a too-large second index quietly shrinks to the end.
question_patterns: How many characters does str1[1:5] of 'Hello World!' return, and what are they?

solution_steps.explain: The span is the stop minus the start.

solution_steps.action: round the span up over the step
solution_steps.explain: Adding step minus 1 before floor division counts every k-th character kept.

concepts.title: Concatenation and Repetition Lengths
concepts.definition: Joining two strings with + forms a new string whose length is the sum of both lengths, and repeating with * multiplies the length by the copy count; neither operation changes the original strings.
concepts.key_idea: Both operators build fresh strings, which is why the originals still print unchanged afterwards.

solution_steps.explain: Each copy repeats the whole joined length.

concepts.title: Sum of Digits Hidden in a String
concepts.definition: A string may carry digit characters among letters; each digit character has an ASCII code 48 more than its face value, so subtracting 48 from the code turns the character into its number before the values are totalled.
concepts.key_idea: Character zero has code 48, so every digit character converts by dropping 48 from its code.

concepts.title: Counting Alphabets, Digits and Symbols in a Line
concepts.definition: Traversing a line character by character sorts each one into a bucket: alphabets, digits, special symbols or whitespace; adding the four bucket counts must reproduce the total character count returned by len().
concepts.key_idea: A counter that increments inside an if branch per category is the standard pattern for this classification.
question_patterns: In the line 'Today is a Holiday', how many times does the character a occur, per the charCount function?
A line has 12 alphabets, 3 digits, 4 special symbols and 5 spaces. What total does len() report?

solution_steps.action: merge the letter and digit buckets
solution_steps.explain: Alphabets and digits are counted first.
Spaces complete the total, which should equal len() of the line.

concepts.title: Built-in Methods for String Manipulation
concepts.definition: Python ships string methods such as upper(), lower(), title(), count(), find(), index(), replace(), split(), join(), partition(), strip() and endswith(); find() answers -1 for a missing substring while index() raises ValueError instead.
concepts.formula: str1.count(word) -> occurrences; str1.find(word) -> first index or -1
concepts.key_idea: Methods never edit the original string; each one hands back a new value because strings cannot change.
question_patterns: What do mySubject.count('e') and mySubject.find('Science') return for 'Computer Science'?

solution_steps.action: apply the method to a copy
solution_steps.explain: Each method inspects or rebuilds the string and returns a new value; the original binding stays intact.

concepts.title: Palindrome Check by Two Indices
concepts.definition: A palindrome reads the same in both directions; the check walks one index from the start and one from the end towards the middle, and any mismatched pair proves the string is not a palindrome.
concepts.formula: front = 0, back = size - 1, move inward until front >= back
concepts.key_idea: Comparing only half the string suffices, because the two indices meet in the middle.
question_patterns: Why is the string 'kanak' a palindrome while 'computer' is not, per checkPalin?

solution_steps.explain: Match position front with position back, stepping both inward; returning False at the first mismatch and True when the indices cross.

worked_examples.q: Checking 'madam' with two indices: how many character pairs must match before the middle is reached?

concepts.title: Immutability and Membership of Strings
concepts.definition: A string cannot be edited in place: assigning to one of its positions raises TypeError, so every apparent change builds a new string; the in and not in operators test whether one string occurs inside another, answering True or False.
concepts.key_idea: Immutability is the reason methods such as replace() must hand back a fresh string rather than patch the old one.
question_patterns: What error appears on executing str1[1] = 'a' for str1 = 'Hello World!'?
What do 'W' in str1 and 'My' in str1 return for 'Hello World!'?

solution_steps.explain: Item assignment on a string raises TypeError; membership operators only read, returning True when the left string occurs inside the right one.
